chains.title: ARID5B binds the ref T allele; alt C disrupts a repressor motif in the dELS

links.claim: ARID5B binds the ref T allele more strongly: the literature states that rs1421085 T-to-C interrupts a conserved ARID5B repressor motif, so the C allele loses ARID5B binding. ARID5B has no QBiC-SELEX model in the supplied rows, so I do not use another TF's SELEX change as its evidence; selection is by the quoted motif-disruption literature, with conservation at the site consistent with a functional motif.

The motif lies in dELS EH38E3181208, a distal enhancer-like element with active chromatin and cofactor occupancy over the variant, consistent with a regulatory element whose output could be altered by loss of ARID5B repression.

FTO is the strongest locus-assigned gene (L2G 0.99) and contains the variant, but no adipose eQTL establishes FTO as the directly regulated gene; IRX3 is a plausible distal target but has only a pancreas eQTL in the supplied data. The target-gene direction in adipose remains unresolved.

The quoted literature ties the allele effect to activated adipocytes and thermogenic/beige-to-white adipocyte state, making subcutaneous adipose/pre-adipocytes the relevant context, although direct pre-adipocyte ARID5B occupancy at this base is not supplied.

Allele-specific loss of ARID5B repression on C can shift adipocyte thermogenesis and thereby influence obesity. The core claim is motif loss on C; however the GWAS evidence in E15 codes T as the effect/risk allele, while the quoted literature implies C disrupts ARID5B repression and may be the functional risk allele, so the disease-risk direction is not settled by the supplied evidence.

predictions: Allele-specific ARID5B binding or reporter assays in pre-adipocytes show stronger ref T binding and C-allele loss of repression.
ARID5B perturbation in pre-adipocytes changes thermogenic/beige-adipocyte programs and, if FTO/IRX3 is the relevant target, changes their expression.
The C allele alters enhancer activity in an ARID5B-motif-dependent manner.
falsified_if: ARID5B does not bind the ref T motif or shows no allele-specific binding in adipose/pre-adipocyte assays.
Disrupting the ARID5B motif has no effect on enhancer activity or adipocyte thermogenic programs.
The phenotype is fully explained by a linked variant rather than by ARID5B binding at this base.

chains.title: No TF-mediated allelic effect; linked or unproven causal variant
predictions: No reproducible allele-specific TF occupancy or enhancer activity from this base in subcutaneous adipose/pre-adipocytes.
Any obesity association is attributable to a linked causal variant or to non-allelic regulatory effects at the FTO/IRX3 locus rather than to rs1421085 itself.
Allele-specific assays at this base show no difference after controlling for linked variants.
falsified_if: Adipose or pre-adipocyte assays show rs1421085 allele-specific TF binding and enhancer activity that tracks with the GWAS effect.
A molecular QTL in adipose maps the causal variant to this base and is disrupted by the allele.

chains.title: ATF3 binds the alt C allele more and represses FTO

links.claim: ATF3 has its own QBiC-SELEX model and the alt C allele binds more strongly (z 21.73, effect +1.403, strong site), and ATF3 is highly expressed in adipose. However, the only ENCODE ATF3 peak over the variant is in HCT116, not adipose; E35 explicitly reports no matching subcutaneous-adipose ATF3 ChIP peak, so adipose occupancy is unproven.
The variant lies in dELS EH38E3181208 with active-enhancer cofactor occupancy, so an allele-specific TF change could in principle alter enhancer output.

FTO is the top locus-assigned gene (L2G 0.99), but the only FTO eQTL is in skeletal muscle (alt C NES +0.14), and there is no significant subcutaneous adipose eQTL for this variant; adipose target-gene direction is not established.
Subcutaneous adipose/pre-adipocytes are the expression context and ATF3 is highly expressed there, but no adipose/pre-adipocyte ChIP-seq or functional assay over this variant is available.

This chain requires ATF3 to repress FTO so that protective C binding more lowers FTO and reduces obesity. No supplied evidence shows ATF3 represses FTO, and the muscle FTO eQTL has alt C increasing FTO, creating a direction conflict.

predictions: Adipose/pre-adipocyte ChIP or reporter assays show C-allele-specific ATF3 occupancy at this element.
ATF3 knockdown or overexpression changes FTO expression in the repression direction.
The C allele lowers FTO in adipose if this chain is correct.
falsified_if: Adipose assays show no ATF3 binding or no allelic difference at rs1421085.
ATF3 activation increases FTO or IRX3 rather than repressing it.
Adipose eQTL or reporter data show the C allele increases FTO/IRX3 in a way incompatible with the GWAS risk direction.

chains.title: FOXP1 binds the ref T allele more and activates FTO

links.claim: FOXP1 shows ref T binding more in QBiC-SELEX (z -16.49, effect -1.476, strong ref site), but the best model is a CIS-BP-mapped FOXC2 model rather than an own FOXP1 model, and the only cited occupancy is in HepG2, not adipose. The binding evidence is therefore indirect and not in the relevant cell type.
The variant lies in dELS EH38E3181208 with active-enhancer marks, supporting element context only.
FTO is strongly locus-assigned (L2G 0.99), but the only FTO eQTL is skeletal muscle with alt C NES +0.14, and no adipose eQTL establishes FTO direction.
FOXP1 is expressed in GTEx subcutaneous adipose, but no adipose/pre-adipocyte ChIP-seq or functional assay over the variant is supplied.

This chain requires FOXP1 to activate FTO so that risk T with more FOXP1 raises FTO and obesity. No supplied evidence supports FOXP1 activation of FTO, and FOXP1 is often a repressor; the direction is conditional and atypical.

predictions: Adipose/pre-adipocyte assays show T-allele-specific FOXP1 occupancy at this element.
FOXP1 perturbation increases FTO expression if FOXP1 acts as an activator here.
The T allele is associated with higher FTO in adipose if this chain is correct.
falsified_if: FOXP1 does not occupy this element in adipose/pre-adipocytes.
FOXP1 represses FTO or IRX3 in this context, making the direction incompatible with T as the risk allele.
Functional assays show no T-allele-specific FOXP1 effect.

grades_v0.reason: ATF3 has an own QBiC-SELEX model and the alt C allele binds more strongly (z 21.73, effect +1.403, strong site), but the only cited ENCODE occupancy is in HCT116, not subcutaneous adipose/pre-adipocytes, and there is no quoted allele-specific assay in the relevant context. Under the binding rule this is one of the two required evidence types, so weak.

E03/E04 directly place rs1421085 in dELS EH38E3181208 and show active-enhancer cofactor occupancy over the variant (e.g. EP300, MED1, POLR2A, KAT2B). This supports the element annotation, although no allele-specific reporter or adipose-specific activity assay is cited.

FTO has strong locus assignment (L2G 0.99) and the variant lies in the FTO gene body, but the only cited FTO eQTL is in skeletal muscle (alt C NES +0.14) and the only other eQTL is IRX3 in pancreas. No adipose/pre-adipocyte eQTL or perturbation establishes FTO as the target or its direction in the stated context.

ATF3 is highly expressed in GTEx subcutaneous adipose (57.63 TPM, rank 88) and the element is annotated dELS, but GTEx adipose is a proxy for pre-adipocytes and no adipose/pre-adipocyte ChIP-seq or functional assay at this variant is cited.

T is the GWAS effect/risk allele, and the chain's direction requires ATF3 to repress FTO so that alt C binding more lowers FTO and reduces obesity. No cited evidence shows ATF3 represses FTO; moreover the available FTO muscle eQTL has alt C increasing FTO, opposite to the required C-lowering effect if FTO is the causal target.

JUN has an own QBiC-SELEX model and alt C binds more strongly (z 17.91, effect +0.317, strong site), but ENCODE occupancy over the variant is only in HepG2, not adipose/pre-adipocytes, and no relevant allele-specific assay is cited.
E03/E04 support the dELS EH38E3181208 annotation and active cofactor occupancy over this variant. This is direct element-context support, but not evidence of allele-specific enhancer output.

FTO is strongly locus-assigned (L2G 0.99) and is the gene-body gene, but the cited eQTL evidence is FTO in skeletal muscle and IRX3 in pancreas, not adipose/pre-adipocytes. Target-gene direction in the stated context remains unestablished.
JUN is extremely highly expressed in GTEx subcutaneous adipose (442.88 TPM, rank 3), but no adipose/pre-adipocyte ENCODE ChIP-seq peak over the variant or functional assay is cited.

The chain requires JUN/AP-1 to repress FTO so that protective C increases JUN binding and lowers FTO. No cited evidence supports JUN repression of FTO, and AP-1 is often activating; the muscle FTO eQTL direction (alt C higher FTO) further conflicts with the required C-lowering effect.

TEAD1 has an own QBiC-SELEX model and alt C binds more strongly (z 21.23, effect +1.544, strong site), but the cited ENCODE occupancy is only in HepG2, not adipose/pre-adipocytes, and no allele-specific assay in the relevant cell type is quoted.
E03/E04 place the variant in dELS EH38E3181208 with active-enhancer cofactor marks. This supports the element annotation, but not an allele-specific TEAD1-dependent enhancer effect.

FTO has strong L2G support, but the only cited FTO eQTL is in skeletal muscle and shows alt C NES +0.14; no adipose eQTL or perturbation establishes FTO direction in the stated context. IRX3 is also nearby and has only a pancreas eQTL.
TEAD1 is expressed in GTEx adipose (40.88 TPM, rank 148), but there is no adipose/pre-adipocyte ChIP-seq occupancy or functional assay over the variant.

The phenotype direction only works if TEAD1 lowers FTO/IRX3 or another obesity-promoting target from the alt C allele. No cited evidence supports that; if TEAD1 activates FTO, alt C binding more would be expected to increase FTO and conflict with T being the GWAS risk allele.

FOXP1 shows ref T binding more in QBiC-SELEX (z -16.49, effect -1.476), but the best model is a CIS-BP-mapped FOXC2 model rather than a FOXP1 own model, and the only cited occupancy is in HepG2. The binding evidence is therefore indirect and not in the relevant cell type.
E03/E04 directly support that the variant lies in dELS EH38E3181208 with active-enhancer cofactors. This supports element context only; no allele-specific enhancer assay is cited.
FTO is strongly locus-assigned (L2G 0.99) and contains the variant, but the only cited FTO eQTL is skeletal muscle with alt C NES +0.14, and there is no adipose/pre-adipocyte eQTL or perturbation.
FOXP1 is expressed in GTEx adipose (14.95 TPM, rank 419), but no adipose/pre-adipocyte ChIP-seq or functional assay over the variant is cited.

The chain requires FOXP1 to activate FTO so that risk T with more FOXP1 binding raises FTO and obesity. No cited evidence supports FOXP1 activation of FTO, and FOXP1 is often a repressor; the direction is therefore conditional and atypical.

grades_final.reason: ARID5B binding to the ref T allele is supported only by literature motif-disruption statements (E37a/E37b) plus conservation (E01). There is no ARID5B ChIP over the variant in subcutaneous adipose/pre-adipocytes and no ARID5B QBiC-SELEX row, so this is indirect and not an occupancy assay.

E03 directly places the variant in dELS EH38E3181208, and E04 shows many ENCODE TF/cofactor peaks over the variant in some biosamples. The element annotation and active-cofactor context are supported, although adipose-specific occupancy is not.

FTO is strongly locus-assigned by L2G (E16) and contains the variant (E02), but there is no significant subcutaneous adipose eQTL (E36); the only FTO eQTL is skeletal muscle (E17). This supports locus assignment, not adipose-specific FTO regulation.

E37b directly ties the rs1421085 effect to activated thermogenic/beige adipocytes derived from human abdominal subcutaneous adipose, supporting subcutaneous adipose as the relevant context; pre-adipocyte ARID5B occupancy itself remains unproven.

E37a/E37b support an adipocyte thermogenic mechanism and E15 supports obesity association, but the risk-allele direction is inconsistent: E15 reports T as the effect/risk allele, while the ARID5B motif-loss literature implies C is the functional allele. The phenotype direction is therefore unresolved.

ATF3 has an own-model QBiC-SELEX change in the stated direction (E20), but occupancy is only reported in HCT116, not subcutaneous adipose/pre-adipocytes; E35 explicitly reports no matching adipose ATF3 peak. One of the two required binding evidence types is present, so weak.

E03 directly annotates the variant in dELS EH38E3181208 and E04 shows cofactor/TF occupancy over the variant in ENCODE biosamples, supporting an active regulatory element context, though not adipose-specific occupancy.

FTO is the top L2G gene (E16), but there is no subcutaneous adipose eQTL for this variant (E36); the only FTO eQTL is skeletal muscle with alt C increasing FTO (E17). Adipose-specific target-gene direction is not established.

ATF3 is expressed in subcutaneous adipose (E20), but there is no adipose/pre-adipocyte ChIP-seq or functional assay over the variant; E35 reports absence of matching adipose ATF3 peaks. Expression context alone is indirect.

No cited evidence shows ATF3 represses FTO or that the alt C allele lowers FTO/obesity. The muscle FTO eQTL has alt C increasing FTO (E17), creating a direction conflict with the proposed protective-C/lower-FTO mechanism.

FOXP1 QBiC-SELEX supports stronger ref T binding (E23), but the best model is a CIS-BP-mapped FOXC2 model and the only cited occupancy is HepG2, not subcutaneous adipose/pre-adipocytes. This is indirect and not cell-type-matched.
E03 directly places the variant in dELS EH38E3181208 and E04 shows active-enhancer cofactor/TF occupancy over the variant in ENCODE biosamples, supporting element identity and activity context.

FTO is strongly L2G-assigned (E16), but the only FTO eQTL is skeletal muscle (E17) and there is no subcutaneous adipose eQTL (E36); adipose-specific regulation of FTO by this element is not established.
FOXP1 is expressed in GTEx subcutaneous adipose (E23), but no adipose/pre-adipocyte ChIP-seq or functional assay over the variant is supplied, so cell-type relevance is expression-context only.

No cited evidence shows FOXP1 activates FTO, and FOXP1 is often a repressor; the required T-allele-more-FOXP1-leading-to-higher-FTO-and-obesity direction is unsupported and atypical. E15 association alone does not supply this mechanistic link.

checks.why: Directly tests whether ATF3 occupies this variant in the stated adipose context; this is the top-ranked chain's weakest essential link.
Tests whether FTO or IRX3 has an adipose eQTL at this variant and in which direction; this would affect the gene and phenotype links of H1-H4.
Searches for quoted perturbation or reporter evidence that ATF3 represses FTO at this locus; without this, H1's phenotype direction remains conditional.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr16:53767042:T>C, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (GTEx tissue median Adipose - Subcutaneous), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 16 occupied (10 with a strong site), 5 of 157 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 0 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 554 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 3 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
